headline: strong
texts: You came through with no gaps and at most one shaky area. You read the patient and the qualifier before choosing, and that habit is what exams reward. Use the review cards to polish the one shaky item, and revisit the module in a week to check it holds.
Secure: you read 'most common' as frequency, in general and in pregnancy.
Secure: lymphoid hyperplasia for the young, faecolith for adults, and you checked the age.
Secure: you order obstruction to pressure to gangrene and explain the shift of pain, with the end artery in mind.
Secure: you use pain, then vomiting, then fever as a filter against other stories.
Secure: psoas, obturator and Rovsing each sit on the right manoeuvre and the right position.
Secure: you know which Alvarado items score 2 and what 7 or more means.
Secure: you chose the first test by patient: ultrasound for children and pregnancy, CECT for adults.
Secure: beta-hCG first in women and a look-alike list for each group.
Secure: you matched surgery or antibiotics-first to the patient, with the qualifiers.
Secure: regimen for a mass, drainage for an abscess, selective interval surgery.
Secure: you keep disease and operation complications apart and name the ilioinguinal nerve.
Secure: carcinoid is the commonest appendix tumour and you know the 2 cm rule.
Your Sure taps matched your answers. That is a useful signal: trust Sure when you can state a reason, and treat Guessing as a prompt to review that card.
You took a fast lane after a correct, confident answer and skipped some teaching. Check the objectives listed as shaky or gap: if the skipped topic appears there, review its card.
No gaps showed. Keep the schedule of review cards at 1, 3, 7, 21 and 60 days and practise mixed-age imaging and management stems to stay sharp.
